entries.title: Principles of Microbiology (Bacteriology, Virology, Mycology, Parasitology, Transmission)

testable_competencies.classification: Classify an infectious agent by broad category (bacteria/virus/fungus/parasite) and basic transmission mechanism, as background for every disease-specific unit later in the chapter.

entries.zero_question_reason: Foundational microbiology background, not independently testable; frames the condition-specific units that follow.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 27 (Dyspnea) is the closest presentation-based MCC anchor for pneumonia's cardinal symptom; the objective's diagnostic approach to dyspnea encompasses infectious pulmonary causes including pneumonia, though pneumonia itself is not separately named.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 18 (Cough) causal_conditions lists 'Infectious' under acute cough, the presenting symptom through which pneumonia is most commonly recognized.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose community-acquired and nosocomial pneumonia, assess severity (e.g., using a validated clinical prediction rule), and initiate appropriate empiric management.
testable_competencies.prevention: Recommend influenza/pneumococcal vaccination per Public Health Agency of Canada guidance to reduce pneumonia risk.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Annual influenza vaccination is a named example within objective 74-2's scope; body-confirmed at pdf 726/ID9 ('vaccine for influenza A and B annually for all ages').

testable_competencies.prevention: Recommend annual influenza vaccination per PHAC guidance.
testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize influenza's clinical presentation and differentiate from other respiratory infections (e.g., COVID-19).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: COVID-19 pneumonia/respiratory failure presents primarily as dyspnea, mapped to objective 27's diagnostic-approach scope.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: COVID-19's population-level spread and public health response fits objective 78-5's outbreak-management competency (case identification, reporting, control measures).

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize COVID-19's clinical presentation and identify patients eligible for antiviral therapy based on risk factors for severe outcomes.
testable_competencies.public_health: Apply outbreak-management and infection-control principles to COVID-19 in institutional settings.

entries.title: Skin and Soft Tissue Infections (Cellulitis, Necrotizing Fasciitis, Acquired Oral Lesions)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 38's causal_conditions explicitly lists 'Infectious' among skin/integument causes, and its key objective requires diagnosing cause/severity/complications of a skin condition - cellulitis and oral candidiasis are canonical examples.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 50-3's causal_conditions names 'Infection (e.g., osteomyelitis, necrotizing fasciitis)' explicitly under acute localized pain, directly naming necrotizing fasciitis as a must-recognize surgical emergency.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize cellulitis and distinguish it from the surgical emergency of necrotizing fasciitis based on clinical red flags (pain out of proportion, rapid progression, systemic toxicity).
testable_competencies.diagnosis: Differentiate oral candidiasis from oral squamous cell carcinoma based on risk factors and morphology.

entries.title: Gastrointestinal Infections (Cross-Reference Only)

testable_competencies.cross_reference: Recognize that infectious GI topics (traveller's diarrhea, chronic diarrhea, H. pylori peptic ulcer disease) are covered under Gastroenterology/Pediatrics, not as independent ID-chapter content.

entries.zero_question_reason: This node carries no independent clinical content in the ID chapter; body-confirmed as pure cross-references to Gastroenterology (G13/G18/G19/G31) and Pediatrics (P44). Testable content is scoped under those chapters, not here.
entries.cross_discipline_note: Cross-references Gastroenterology (G, completed) and Pediatrics (P, not yet mapped) for the actual GI-infection content.

entries.title: Bone and Joint Infections (Septic Arthritis, Diabetic Foot Infections, Osteomyelitis)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 50-3's causal_conditions explicitly names 'osteomyelitis' under infectious causes of acute localized musculoskeletal pain.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Oligoarthralgia (pain in one to four joints)
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 50-1's causal_conditions names 'Infection' under acute joint pain, and its key objective requires determining acuity/severity and need for immediate management - directly matching septic arthritis's medical-emergency status body-confirmed in Toronto Notes.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize septic arthritis as a medical emergency requiring urgent joint aspiration and empiric antibiotics before joint destruction occurs.
testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose diabetic foot infection severity and osteomyelitis (probe-to-bone test, imaging) to guide antibiotic duration and surgical referral.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 62's differential for pathologic murmurs (e.g., new regurgitant murmur) is the presentation through which infective endocarditis is most commonly recognized clinically, though endocarditis is not separately named in the objective's causal_conditions excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Infective endocarditis is a classic cause of unexplained fever with a new murmur; objective 107-1's approach to fever encompasses this presentation.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Recognize infective endocarditis in a patient with new/changing murmur, fever, and risk factors (IVDU, prosthetic valve, prior IE).
testable_competencies.prevention: Identify indications for antibiotic prophylaxis prior to dental/respiratory procedures in high-risk cardiac patients.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 58-1's causal_conditions explicitly names 'Infectious (e.g., meningitis, encephalitis)' as a cause of diffuse disease/coma.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 107-1's key_objectives explicitly instructs candidates to 'rule out life-threatening conditions (e.g., meningococcal meningitis)' when evaluating fever - a near-exact match.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 92's causal_conditions names 'encephalitis' explicitly among primary neurological causes of seizure.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize bacterial meningitis as a medical emergency and initiate empiric antibiotics without delay for imaging/LP when clinically indicated.
testable_competencies.diagnosis: Interpret CSF findings to differentiate bacterial, viral, and other causes of meningitis/encephalitis.

entries.title: Generalized Tetanus

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize generalized tetanus (trismus, opisthotonus) in an under-immunized patient with a contaminated wound, and assess tetanus immunization status/need for prophylaxis after injury.

entries.zero_question_reason: Supports the tetanus-status and prophylaxis actions explicitly required by wound and immunization objectives, but generalized tetanus recognition is not independently anchored in the canonical registry.

entries.title: Rabies

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 109-12 explicitly requires assessing rabies transmission risk after a bite and determining the need for prophylaxis; this anchors the unit's exposure-recognition and post-exposure-prophylaxis competency without implying coverage of advanced clinical rabies management.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize rabies exposure risk (bat/wildlife bite) and the indications for post-exposure prophylaxis (rabies immunoglobulin plus vaccine series).

entries.zero_question_reason: Objective 109-12 anchors exposure assessment and prophylaxis only; no standalone minimum is assigned here before question allocation.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 9-2's causal_conditions explicitly names 'Sepsis' under Distributive shock, and its key objective (diagnose cause, recognize urgency, initiate timely management) is a near-exact match for sepsis recognition and management.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Sepsis is a life-threatening cause of fever; objective 107-1's fever-evaluation approach includes recognizing this severity spectrum.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize sepsis and septic shock, including patients with refractory shock unresponsive to fluids and vasopressors.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate timely sepsis bundle management (cultures, fluids, empiric antibiotics, source control).

entries.title: Leprosy (Hansen's Disease)

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize leprosy as a rare, travel/immigration-associated cause of skin lesions and peripheral neuropathy in Canadian practice.

entries.zero_question_reason: No MCC objective addresses leprosy; exceedingly rare in Canadian generalist practice and appropriately treated as specialist detail rather than core MCCQE content.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: No MCC objective is titled for Lyme disease or tick-borne illness; the nearest adjacent evidence is objective 107-1's general infectious-fever causal category and its enabling objective's mention of travel/exposure history, which does not name Lyme disease specifically.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize erythema migrans and staged Lyme disease presentations in a patient with tick exposure in an endemic Canadian region, and interpret Public-Health-Lab Lyme serology.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: TSS is a distributive-shock presentation matching objective 9-2's scope, though 'toxic shock syndrome' is not itself named in the objective's causal_conditions excerpt (only 'Sepsis' and 'Anaphylaxis' are named).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: TSS presents with precipitous fever, matching objective 107-1's evaluation-of-fever scope.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize toxic shock syndrome in a patient with fever, rash, hypotension, and multiorgan involvement, with attention to tampon-associated and surgical-wound risk factors.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Cat scratch disease's hallmark presentation is regional tender lymphadenopathy 14-21 days after a cat scratch/bite; objective 54's 'Infectious (e.g., viral)' causal category for diffuse/localized lymphadenopathy is the closest match, though Bartonella is not itself named.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize cat scratch disease (Bartonella henselae) in a patient with regional lymphadenopathy and a history of cat scratch/bite exposure, including disseminated presentations in advanced HIV.

entries.title: Syphilis

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 113's key_objectives explicitly requires the candidate to 'distinguish sexually transmitted infection (STI) from other causes' - syphilis is a classic STI in this differential, though not itself named in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Congenital syphilis's classic stigmata (saddle nose, Hutchinson's teeth) are dysmorphic features; this objective's scope is a loose secondary anchor for that portion only, not for adult/staged syphilis generally.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose staged syphilis (primary/secondary/latent/tertiary/neurosyphilis) using the Public-Health-Lab serology algorithm and recognize congenital syphilis stigmata.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate benzathine penicillin G per stage; recognize indications for LP in suspected neurosyphilis.

entries.cross_discipline_note: Overlaps Gynecology (GY, completed - SU-GY-17 Sexually Transmitted Infections notes this same cross-discipline gap) and Family Medicine (FM, not yet mapped, cited in-text for generalized STI workup); ownership deferred to the global cross-chapter overlap audit.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Chronic cough is the cardinal presenting symptom of pulmonary TB; objective 18's 'Chronic cough' causal category includes 'Postinfectious' etiologies, though TB is not itself named in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: TB is a reportable disease requiring Public Health contact tracing and outbreak-style management in institutional exposures, matching objective 78-5's scope.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Differentiate latent TB infection from active pulmonary/extrapulmonary/miliary TB, and select TST vs. IGRA screening appropriately.
testable_competencies.management: Recognize RIPE first-line therapy and the clinical indicators of MDR/XDR-TB requiring specialist referral.
testable_competencies.public_health: Recognize TB as a reportable disease requiring Public Health notification and contact investigation.

entries.title: HIV Infection: Epidemiology, Transmission, Natural History, and Antiretroviral Therapy Overview

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Fever in the immune compromised host / recurrent fever
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 107-4 is scoped exactly to patients with immunodeficiency and fever; HIV is the paradigmatic chronic immunodeficiency this objective addresses, and the objective's rationale ('patients with immunodeficiencies are at high risk for infections... depend on type and severity of immunosuppression') directly frames HIV's natural-history-driven opportunistic-infection risk.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 107-1's enabling objectives explicitly name 'immunocompromised state due to HIV' as a host factor to elicit on history when evaluating fever.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose acute retroviral syndrome and interpret the relationship between CD4 count, viral load, and disease stage.
testable_competencies.risk_assessment: Identify modes of HIV transmission and per-exposure-route risk to guide counselling and post-exposure decisions.
testable_competencies.management: Recognize the general classes of antiretroviral therapy and their role in reducing transmission risk (without encoding a specific current regimen, which is current-guidance-sensitive).

entries.title: HIV Testing, Pre/Post-Test Counselling, and Prevention (PrEP/PEP)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: HIV screening and pre-exposure prophylaxis counselling fit objective 74's scope of age/risk-factor-based preventive health advice and screening investigations, though HIV is not itself named in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: HIV pre- and post-test counselling is fundamentally an informed-consent process (assessing risk, informed decision to be tested); objective 121-1's general consent framework is a loose secondary anchor, not an HIV-specific match.

testable_competencies.testing: Differentiate nominal, non-nominal, and anonymous HIV testing pathways and their Public Health notification obligations.
testable_competencies.counselling: Provide appropriate pre- and post-test HIV counselling addressing stigma, risk assessment, and connection to support services.
testable_competencies.prevention: Recognize indications for and general concept of pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) and post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP), without encoding a specific current regimen.

entries.title: Endemic Mycoses (Histoplasmosis, Blastomycosis, Coccidioidomycosis)

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize endemic mycoses (Histoplasma, Blastomyces, Coccidioides) as regional/occupational-exposure causes of pulmonary or disseminated fungal disease, particularly in immunocompromised or travel-exposed patients.

entries.zero_question_reason: No MCC objective addresses endemic mycoses specifically; low generalist yield outside specific geographic/occupational exposure contexts.

entries.title: Opportunistic Fungi (Pneumocystis Jirovecii Pneumonia, Cryptococcus, Candida, Aspergillus)

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Fever in the immune compromised host / recurrent fever
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 107-4's causal-conditions framework for fever in an immunocompromised host directly encompasses PJP, cryptococcal, candidal, and aspergillus infections as organism classes tied to specific immune defects (e.g., cellular immunodeficiency/HIV, neutropenia).

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: PJP's presenting symptom is dyspnea in an immunocompromised host; objective 27's general dyspnea-diagnostic scope is a loose secondary anchor, as PJP is not itself named in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize PJP, cryptococcal, candidal, and aspergillus infections as opportunistic diseases in HIV/immunocompromised hosts and initiate appropriate empiric management.
testable_competencies.prevention: Recognize CD4-threshold-based prophylaxis concepts for opportunistic infections (without encoding a specific current regimen).

entries.title: Fungal Infections: Superficial and Dermatophyte (Cross-Reference Only)

testable_competencies.cross_reference: Recognize that superficial fungal infections and dermatophytes are covered under Dermatology, not as independent ID-chapter content.

entries.zero_question_reason: Body-confirmed as pure cross-references to Dermatology (D31-D49); no independent clinical content exists in this chapter.
entries.cross_discipline_note: Cross-references Dermatology (D, completed) for the actual clinical content.

entries.title: Subcutaneous Fungal Infections (Sporotrichosis)

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize sporotrichosis (nodular lymphangitis) in a patient with an occupational soil/plant-matter inoculation injury (e.g., gardening, rose thorn).

entries.zero_question_reason: No MCC objective addresses sporotrichosis; low-yield occupational-exposure topic appropriately treated as specialist detail.

entries.title: Parasitic Infections: Protozoa (Entamoeba, Giardia, Trichomonas, Cryptosporidium)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 22-1's causal_conditions names 'Parasites' generically under infectious acute diarrhea; Entamoeba, Giardia, and Cryptosporidium are the classic parasitic causes, though none is individually named in the retrieved excerpt.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Trichomonas vaginalis is a classic cause of vaginal discharge; objective 113's STI-differentiation scope covers this pathogen, though it is not individually named in the retrieved excerpt.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose amoebiasis, giardiasis, trichomoniasis, and cryptosporidiosis based on exposure history and stool/wet-mount findings.
testable_competencies.management: Initiate appropriate antiparasitic therapy (e.g., metronidazole) for the relevant protozoal infection.

entries.title: Blood and Tissue Infections (Malaria, Trypanosoma cruzi, Toxoplasma gondii)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 107-1's causal_conditions explicitly names 'Parasitic (e.g., Plasmodium)' as an infectious cause of fever - a direct, named match for malaria.

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Fever in the immune compromised host / recurrent fever
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Toxoplasma reactivation is a classic opportunistic infection in advanced HIV, matching objective 107-4's immunocompromised-host-fever scope.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Diagnose malaria in a febrile returned traveller and recognize the need for urgent species identification and treatment.
testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize Toxoplasma gondii reactivation as an opportunistic CNS infection in advanced HIV.

entries.title: Helminths (Roundworms, Flatworms, Schistosoma spp.)

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize helminthic infections (nematodes, cestodes/trematodes, schistosomiasis) as travel/exposure-associated causes of eosinophilia and organ-specific disease.

entries.zero_question_reason: No MCC objective addresses helminthic infections specifically; low generalist yield outside specific travel/exposure contexts, appropriately treated as specialist detail.

entries.title: Ectoparasites (Cross-Reference Only)

testable_competencies.cross_reference: Recognize that scabies and lice are covered under Dermatology, not as independent ID-chapter content.

entries.zero_question_reason: Body-confirmed as a pure cross-reference to Dermatology D33; no independent clinical content exists in this chapter.
entries.cross_discipline_note: Cross-references Dermatology (D, completed) for the actual clinical content.

entries.title: Travel Medicine (General Travel Precautions, Fever in the Returned Traveller)

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Objective 107-1's enabling objectives explicitly require eliciting 'travel history (e.g., locations, timing, use of chemoprophylaxis)' when evaluating fever - a near-exact match for this unit's core competency.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Pre-travel vaccination and malaria chemoprophylaxis counselling fits objective 74-2's immunization-advice scope.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Take a structured travel/exposure history and generate a differential for fever in the returned traveller (malaria, enteric fever, dengue, and other vector-borne illnesses).
testable_competencies.prevention: Advise on pre-travel vaccination, malaria chemoprophylaxis, and food/water precautions.

mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: Fever of unknown origin is a defined diagnostic-approach subtype of objective 107-1's general fever-evaluation scope, sharing its key objective to diagnose cause, severity, and complications of unexplained fever.

testable_competencies.diagnosis: Apply a systematic diagnostic approach (repeated history, exposures, infectious contacts, targeted investigations) to fever of unknown origin.

entries.title: Infections in the Immunocompromised Host (Febrile Neutropenia, Solid Organ Transplant Recipients, IRIS)

mcc_evidence.objective_title: Fever in the immune compromised host / recurrent fever
mcc_evidence.official_source: research/mcc/objectives_registry.json (retrieved from official MCC Objectives Online Web Service)
mcc_evidence.mapping_rationale: This is a near-exact, near-identical-title match: objective 107-4 is scoped precisely to fever in the immune-compromised host, directly covering febrile neutropenia, solid-organ-transplant infection risk, and IRIS.

testable_competencies.recognition: Recognize febrile neutropenia as an oncologic emergency requiring urgent empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics.
testable_competencies.diagnosis: Determine the underlying immune defect (neutropenia, transplant immunosuppression, ART-related immune reconstitution) and the likely class of causative organism.
testable_competencies.recognition_iris: Recognize immune reconstitution inflammatory syndrome (IRIS) as a diagnosis of exclusion following ART initiation.

entries.title: Antimicrobial Reference Tables and Chapter Bibliography

testable_competencies.reference: Recognize antimicrobial drug classes and general spectrum-of-coverage concepts as background reference material; specific current antibiotic/antifungal/antiparasitic choice, dose, and duration are deliberately not scope-mapped here.

entries.zero_question_reason: Pure drug-class reference tables and chapter bibliography (including a cross-reference to Family Medicine FM54 and a clinical-trials bibliography); per project instructions, exact current antibiotic/antifungal/antiparasitic choice, dose, and duration are not encoded into the scope layer and are deliberately excluded from question planning. Clinical answers will be researched from current Canadian guidance during question generation for the disease-specific units that reference this material (e.g., SU-ID-05, SU-ID-07, SU-ID-09, SU-ID-12, SU-ID-18, SU-ID-19).
